newsitem.title: UK: UK admits failings in applying Rwandan arms ban.
newsitem.headline: UK admits failings in applying Rwandan arms ban.

text.p: Britain said on Tuesday it was tightening procedures to plug gaps in its implementation of global arms embargoes, which it admitted had been patchy.

The government, in a report on the UN ban on arms exports to Rwanda, admitted it had failed to implement the embargo in two "crown dependencies" -- the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands -- due to shortcomings by the Home Office (interior ministry).
"There was a deficiency in the procedures. The Home Office didn't attach sufficient priority to it," one official said.
The report was drafted by an inter-ministerial committee set up last year after media reports that some British companies had broken the embargo by selling arms to Rwandan extremists in Zaire.
One company named in the reports was Mil-Tec Corp registered in the Isle of Man, an island off Britain's north-west coast.
The government said it could not comment directly on the allegations as they were being probed by Customs investigators.

But it said any gaps in controls in the Isle of Man were narrow -- direct arms exports from the island to Rwanda were prohibited but trafficking by companies registered there but operating in third countries was not.

The government said it had since closed this gap in the Isle of Man's controls but was still considering whether legislation was needed to prohibit arms trafficking by British nationals, adding that the main problem would be enforcing such a law.
The main opposiiton Labour party accused the government of committing serious errors in implementing the Rwandan embargo.
"They have shown extreme sloppiness and a lack of urgency. It must never be allowed to happen again," Labour's defence spokesman, David Clark, said.
